title.text: Budapest: Hungarian Cooking Class with Historic Market Walk

pills.label: 3–4 hours
pills.pop_html: Duration: 3–4 hours.

pills.label: English instructor
pills.pop_html: Instructor speaks English.

Market part: A guided walk through Budapest's historic Central Market Hall, tasting local treats and buying fresh seasonal ingredients, then on to the nearby apartment-style kitchen. An Evening Cooking Class option skips the market.
What you cook: A traditional Hungarian main course and a dessert from simple family recipes. Dishes change slightly with what is fresh and in season, and you eat them together around one table.
Drinks: A welcome shot of pálinka, wine pairing during the class and a Hungarian spirit tasting. Non-drinkers get a non-alcoholic substitute.
While you cook: Welcome tastings of Hungarian cold cuts, cheeses and pickles, and you go home with a recipe booklet and a vintage postcard.

pills.label: What's included
pills.pop_html: Included: Guided market tour at the Central Market Hall; Hands-on Hungarian cooking class in a local apartment; Local English-speaking chef and host; All fresh ingredients and cooking equipment; Welcome tastings of cold cuts, cheeses and pickles.

best_for.pick_html: for the most complete food experience for the money: market walk, a main and dessert, cold cuts, wine and pálinka for €90, about €22–30 an hour.
best_for.skip_html: if you have coeliac disease: the kitchen cannot rule out cross-contamination.

items.a: Depends on the option you choose (market or evening class), shown when you check availability.

Central Market Hall tour, hands-on class with a local English-speaking chef, all ingredients, cold cuts, cheeses and pickles, main course and dessert, wine pairing and spirit tasting, recipe booklet, vintage postcard.

items.q: Can I eat vegetarian or gluten-free?
items.a: Tell them about restrictions beforehand; coeliac disease cannot be accommodated.
Menu shifts with the season, no fixed dish list. Cannot cater for coeliac disease. Meeting point depends on the option you pick.
Market walk and cooking class in one booking. Main course and dessert, eaten family-style. Wine pairing and spirit tasting included.

price.note: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before. The final price shows before you pay.

pills.label: English instructor
pills.pop_html: Instructor speaks English.
You make: One full chimney cake: you roll the dough into strips, wrap it around a wooden spindle, brush it with sugar and bake it in the rotating oven until it caramelises.
Timing: 45 minutes of hands-on workshop, then 20 minutes with your cake and coffee or tea. The dough needs about 75 minutes to rise, so it is ready for you on arrival.
Toppings: Cinnamon sugar, vanilla, cocoa or walnut. The studio uses wheat, orange, milk, nuts and coconut in a small shared space, so skip it if you have any of those allergies.
Kids: Built for families, couples and small groups; 1 adult is required for every 4 children. Everyone gets a certificate of completion.

pills.label: What's included
pills.pop_html: Included: All ingredients and tools; Hands-on kürtőskalács workshop; Apron; One freshly baked chimney cake; Toppings.

pills.label: Skip the ticket queue
pills.pop_html: Skip the ticket queue: your entry is booked in advance.

best_for.pick_html: for the cheapest hands-on taste of Hungary: €20 for an hour of rolling, baking and eating your own kürtőskalács.
best_for.skip_html: if you want to learn the dough itself: it is pre-prepared, so book #9 for dough from scratch.

items.a: Ipar u. 11, 1095 Budapest.
Hands-on workshop, all ingredients and tools, apron, 1 freshly baked chimney cake, toppings, coffee or tea, certificate of completion.
About 15 minutes from the city centre by public transport.
Dough is pre-prepared, not made from scratch. 1 cake per person (Kató Néni gives you 3). About 15 minutes from the centre by public transport.
Cheapest class on the list. Ingredients, tools, apron and coffee or tea included. Family-friendly, 1 adult per 4 children.

price.note: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before. The final price shows before you pay.

What you cook: A traditional 3-course Hungarian meal from scratch. You select your preferred dishes, and the options can include goulash soup and chicken paprikash.
Technique: A local chef explains the flavours and techniques behind Hungarian cooking, including the famous paprika. Recipes come home in a colourful printed booklet.
Drinks: Soft drinks, coffee, tea and a pálinka tasting during the class, then lunch with wine.
Group size: Limited to 10 people. The venue can vary (Páva utca 13 or Bécsi út 27), and the exact address is emailed after booking. No transfers.

best_for.skip_html: if you want a market visit as well: #7 adds one, from the same school, for €40 more.

items.a: Páva u. 13, 1094 Budapest, or Bécsi út 27 (confirmed by email after booking).

Pickup and drop-off.

title.text: Budapest Home Cooking: Goulash and Crêpes with Locals

pills.label: 2.5 hours
pills.pop_html: Duration: 2.5 hours.

pills.label: 3 languages
pills.pop_html: Instructor speaks English, German and Hungarian.

What you cook: Gulyásleves the proper way: why the order of ingredients matters, how to use different Hungarian paprikas, and how to pinch csipetke, the hand-made pasta bits that give the soup its texture.
Dessert: Paper-thin Hungarian pancakes you flip yourself, filled with apricot jam or vanilla cottage cheese. Warm pogácsa, the savoury Hungarian scone, comes first.
Group size: A small group of 6 to 8 guests at most, in a private family home. Hosted in English, German or Hungarian.
Getting there: From Széll Kálmán tér take tram 56, 56A or 61 to the Hűvösvölgy terminus, a 15–20 minute ride into the Buda hills, then walk to Ördögárok utca 14.

pills.label: What's included
pills.pop_html: Included: 2-hour hands-on session with a local host; A large bowl of authentic goulash; Hungarian pancakes with traditional fillings; Hungarian wines or non-alcoholic drinks, coffee; Booklet of recipes.

best_for.pick_html: for learning real goulash with hand-pinched csipetke in a family home, plus palacsinta, in 2.5 hours for €96.
best_for.skip_html: if you want to stay central: the home is a 15–20 minute tram ride into the Buda hills.

items.a: Ördögárok u. 14, 1029 Budapest.
2.5-hour hands-on workshop, goulash, Hungarian pancakes with fillings, Hungarian wine or non-alcoholic drinks, coffee, recipe booklet.
English, German, Hungarian.
Max 8.
Tram 56, 56A or 61 from Széll Kálmán tér to Hűvösvölgy, then a short walk.

pills.label: 4 hours

pills.label: English instructor

Market part: A guided visit to a local market hall with its history, an introduction to basic Hungarian ingredients and a small platter of appetisers such as kolbász and körözött. Transfer to the school is included.
What you cook: A traditional 3-course Hungarian meal, cooked hands-on in a well-equipped cookery school and eaten as lunch. Classes run in the morning.
Drinks: A fruity pálinka on arrival, Unicum before lunch, a glass of wine with the meal, and unlimited soft drinks, coffee and tea.
Group size: Limited to 10 people. Meet at Vámház körút 2 (at the Burger King). For dietary needs, contact the school and they will plan a suitable menu.

best_for.skip_html: if budget matters: at €145 it is the most expensive class here, €40 more than the same school's class without the market.

items.a: Vámház krt. 2, 1052 Budapest (at the Burger King).
Guided market tour, appetiser tasting, transfer to the school, 3-course lunch, unlimited soft drinks, coffee and tea, aprons, a glass of wine with lunch, recipes.
